source_review.notes: Checked current official Linux kernel documentation for administration, self-protection, selftests, KUnit, fault injection, tracing, perf security and sysctl, plus current NIST publications for trustworthy-system engineering, platform firmware resiliency and incident response. All eleven official URLs returned HTTP 200. Kernel interfaces, assurance guidance, the review framework, simplified gate arithmetic and engineering recommendations remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked mandatory-gate set, individual gate outcomes, conjunction, claim, evidence, RPO and RTO notation.
Verified pass percentage is presented as descriptive coverage rather than the readiness decision.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates applicable gate results, evidence chains, recovery-state loss, recovery time and scoped decision validity.

evidence: Counted eleven passing outcomes among twelve gates and recomputed 100*11/12 = 91.67 percent.
Recomputed conjunctive readiness as false and identified device-isolation as the sole blocking gate.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic Python snippet reproduced all five outputs and illustrates noncompensable gates without assessing a real platform.

evidence: Derived readiness as the conjunction over all applicable gate-pass predicates.
Confirmed one fail or unknown makes the conjunction false regardless of the fraction of other passes.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The rule is a declared review policy for mandatory properties, not a probability model or formal proof that a passing review eliminates risk.

evidence: Reviewed malicious tenants, shared-resource exhaustion, stale DMA, syscall parsing, crash consistency, control-plane loss, telemetry loss, compromised kernels and corrupted roots.
Reviewed cold-versus-thermal performance, CPU and device hotplug, partial update, incompatible rollback, stale policy restore, expiring exceptions and evidence-invalidating change.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boot, process, memory, scheduler, concurrency, ABI, filesystem, device, network, virtualization, security, performance, recovery and governance boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced each requirement through mechanism, exact configuration, verification, operational evidence and stated limitation.

Verified identity freezing, negative authority tests, resource charging, persistent ownership, useful-service performance, degraded observability, trustworthy recovery and material-change invalidation.
invariant_checking.notes: The invariant set prevents a configured mechanism, isolated benchmark, backup artifact or risk acceptance from standing in for end-to-end behavior.

evidence: Reviewed fifteen decision, identity, requirement, traceability, authority, interference, state, performance, observability, failure, recovery, change, gate, exception and validity obligations.
Constructed counterexamples for configured-as-effective, namespace-as-complete-isolation, observed-maximum-as-bound, backup-as-recovery and score-as-readiness claims.
proof_review.notes: The chapter defines an assurance review framework, not a formal verification of Linux, hardware, firmware, isolation, performance or recovery.

evidence: Audited uses of ready, pass, proof, isolated, bounded, correct, secure, durable, recovered, verified and approved.
Confirmed specification, documentation, analysis, configuration, effective state, empirical observation, operational evidence, exception and residual risk remain distinct.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: A passing receipt is explicitly scoped and expiring; it is never represented as permanent certification or absence of defects.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-100/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, Python toolchain and environment for gate evaluation.
Reviewed required build, runtime, tenant, workload, counter, trace, fault, crash, ownership, update, recovery, raw-artifact, reviewer and limitation evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing toy establishes gate counting and Boolean aggregation only; it provides no evidence for any real OS gate, kernel, device, tenant, incident or recovery capability.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed an operating-system platform as a composition of boot trust, process and memory semantics, resource isolation, persistent and device state, useful service, observability, change and trustworthy recovery.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable concerns including deployed identity, negative access, resource accounting, scheduling, concurrency, syscall ABI, filesystems, DMA, networking, virtualization, self-protection, saturation, crash capture, recovery drills, updates, findings, exceptions and receipts. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from charter, claims and evidence through all major OS boundaries to failure, recovery, change and accountable decisions, followed by fifteen obligations, fifteen trade-offs, twenty-six misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, Linux kernel maintainer, platform-security assessor, hardware or firmware expert, performance engineer, incident responder, recovery practitioner, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
